issues.title: Issue with copy of Line Decorator
issues.body:
We use the line decorator to put arrows on the polylines.

We use a `base` object for the formatting (`ArrowHeadPattern`), and modify it for each different colored line.

But, instead of copying the base object, we keep changing the original.

In this example, the yellow line arrows were the last to be drawn.  That means all of the line arrows get set to yellow:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/215998811-d5555460-2843-443e-8367-62b1e2a03086.png)

Note: I tried switching from spread operator (`{...}`) to using deepCopy, but it appears there is (somehow) a function embedded in the object, which doesn't get copied properly.

okay, so the issue is only the arrow gets yellow instead of all the line arrow gets yellow. We will get all the line arrow get yellow?

I don't think the issue is about the yellow line in particular. The issue is that the arrows get set to the last custom arrow-head color.

We generate a number of `ArrowHeadPattern` objects, and set the color to the color of the current line.  But, instead of creating new ones, each time we actually edit the previous one.  So, in the above diagram we:
1. generate the blue orders line, with a blue arrowhead
2. generate the red orders line, with a red arrowhead.

But, the second arrowhead actually also edits the first arrowhead - which makes the blue line in the image have red arrows.

Aah, I think I've just fixed it @lebaphi 

Let me push my changes.

Hi @IanMayo, spread syntax effectively goes one level deep while copying an object. Therefore, it may be unsuitable for copying multidimensional object. I suggest we use cloneDeep of lodash.
